notes.definition: Red-shift is the observed increase in the wavelength of light from most distant galaxies. The further away a galaxy is, the faster it is moving away and the bigger the red-shift; this is evidence that the universe is expanding and supports the Big Bang theory.
explanation: When the light from a star or galaxy is split into a spectrum, there are dark lines at particular wavelengths, caused by elements absorbing light. The pattern of lines for each element is known from experiments on Earth. In the light from most distant galaxies, the same pattern of lines is seen, but shifted towards the red end of the spectrum (towards longer wavelengths and lower frequencies). This observed increase in wavelength is called red-shift. It shows that the galaxy is moving away from us (receding).

Astronomers have found that the further away a galaxy is, the bigger its red-shift, so the faster it is moving away. Galaxies in all directions show this. The best explanation is not that we are at the centre of the universe, but that space itself is expanding, carrying galaxies apart. If the universe is expanding, then in the past it must have been much smaller.

The observed red-shift therefore provides evidence that the universe is expanding and supports the Big Bang theory. This theory suggests that the universe began from a very small region that was extremely hot and dense, and has been expanding ever since. Scientists use observations such as red-shift to develop and test theories like this; a theory is accepted when it explains the evidence better than alternatives.

Since 1998, observations of supernovae in very distant galaxies have suggested that these galaxies are receding ever faster: the expansion of the universe is speeding up. This was unexpected, and scientists do not yet fully understand it. There is still much about the universe that is not understood. Observations of how galaxies rotate suggest there is much more mass than we can see, called dark mass (dark matter), and the accelerating expansion suggests there is something called dark energy. Neither has yet been explained.
keyFacts: Red-shift: an observed increase in the wavelength of light from most distant galaxies.
Spectral lines are shifted towards the red end (longer wavelength).
Red-shift shows a galaxy is moving away from us.
The further away a galaxy, the faster it moves away and the bigger its red-shift.
Red-shift is evidence that the universe (space itself) is expanding.
It supports the Big Bang theory: the universe began from a very small, extremely hot and dense region.
Since 1998, supernova observations suggest distant galaxies are receding ever faster.
Dark mass (dark matter) and dark energy are not yet understood.

keyTerms.definition: The observed increase in the wavelength of light from a galaxy that is moving away from us.
Light separated into its different wavelengths, often showing dark absorption lines.
The theory that the universe began from a very small region that was extremely hot and dense and has been expanding ever since.
The idea that space itself is stretching, so galaxies move further apart.
Unseen mass that is suggested by the way galaxies rotate; not yet understood.
An unexplained cause suggested for the accelerating expansion of the universe.

workedExamples.title: Comparing two galaxies
workedExamples.question: Galaxy A shows a bigger red-shift than galaxy B. What can you conclude?
steps: A bigger red-shift means the galaxy is moving away faster.
Galaxies moving away faster are further away.
workedExamples.answer: Galaxy A is moving away faster than galaxy B and is further away.

workedExamples.title: From observation to theory
workedExamples.question: Explain how red-shift supports the Big Bang theory.
steps: Light from distant galaxies is red-shifted, so they are moving away.
More distant galaxies are moving away faster, in all directions, so the universe is expanding.
Running the expansion backwards, the universe was once a very small, extremely hot and dense region.
workedExamples.answer: An expanding universe must have started from a very small, hot, dense region, as the Big Bang theory states.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think red-shift means the galaxy looks red.
misconceptions.right: In fact red-shift means the wavelengths are shifted towards the red end of the spectrum; the galaxy does not have to look red.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the Big Bang was an explosion at one point in space.
misconceptions.right: In fact the theory says space itself has been expanding from a very small, extremely hot and dense region.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think red-shift shows that Earth is at the centre of the universe.
misconceptions.right: In fact every galaxy would see the others moving away, because space is expanding everywhere.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think scientists fully understand the universe.
misconceptions.right: In fact dark mass and dark energy remain unexplained, and the accelerating expansion is not fully understood.

realWorld: Edwin Hubble used red-shift measurements in the 1920s to show that galaxies are moving away from us.
The 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for the 1998 supernova observations showing that the expansion is accelerating.
Large telescopes measure red-shifts of millions of galaxies to map the structure of the universe.
separateOnlyContent: This whole subtopic is in separate Physics (8463) only, not Combined Science.

Explain qualitatively the red-shift of light from galaxies that are receding, that the change of each galaxy's speed with distance is evidence of an expanding universe, and how red-shift provides evidence for the Big Bang model.
Explain how scientists use observations to arrive at theories such as the Big Bang, and that much about the universe (dark mass and dark energy) is not yet understood.
examTips: Define red-shift precisely: 'an observed increase in the wavelength of light from distant galaxies'.
Link three ideas in order: further away, faster moving away, bigger red-shift; then conclude the universe is expanding.
When describing the Big Bang, use the words 'very small region', 'extremely hot and dense' and 'expanding'.
If asked about what is not understood, name dark mass (dark matter) and dark energy, and the accelerating expansion seen since 1998.
summary: Light from distant galaxies is red-shifted: wavelength increased.
Red-shift shows galaxies are moving away.
Further galaxies move away faster, with bigger red-shift.
This is evidence the universe is expanding and supports the Big Bang.
Since 1998, distant galaxies seem to be receding ever faster.
Dark mass and dark energy are not yet explained.

questions.question: What is red-shift?
options: A decrease in the wavelength of light from distant galaxies
Galaxies turning red as they age
An increase in the wavelength of light from distant galaxies
markScheme: 1 mark: An increase in the wavelength of light from distant galaxies
questions.explanation: Red-shift is the observed increase in wavelength, shifting spectral lines towards the red end.

questions.question: Which way are the absorption lines shifted in light from a distant galaxy?
markScheme: 1 mark: Towards the red end
questions.explanation: The lines move towards the red end, which has longer wavelengths.

questions.question: What does red-shift tell us about a galaxy?
options: It is moving away from us
markScheme: 1 mark: It is moving away from us
questions.explanation: Red-shift shows the galaxy is receding (moving away).

questions.question: Which theory does red-shift provide evidence for?
markScheme: 1 mark: The Big Bang theory
questions.explanation: Red-shift shows the universe is expanding, which supports the Big Bang theory.

questions.question: Galaxy X is further from Earth than galaxy Y. How does the red-shift of X compare with that of Y?
markScheme: 1 mark: Bigger
questions.explanation: More distant galaxies move away faster, so they show a bigger red-shift.

questions.question: According to the Big Bang theory, how did the universe begin?
options: From a very small region that was extremely hot and dense
From the explosion of a star
It has always been the same size
markScheme: 1 mark: From a very small region that was extremely hot and dense
questions.explanation: The Big Bang theory states the universe began from a very small, extremely hot and dense region and has been expanding since.

questions.question: What happens to the frequency of light that has been red-shifted?
markScheme: 1 mark: It decreases
questions.explanation: A longer wavelength means a lower frequency, because the speed of light is the same.

questions.question: What did observations of supernovae since 1998 suggest?
options: Distant galaxies are receding ever faster
markScheme: 1 mark: Distant galaxies are receding ever faster
questions.explanation: Distant supernovae suggest that the expansion of the universe is accelerating, which is not yet fully understood.

questions.question: Why does red-shift in all directions NOT mean that the Earth is at the centre of the universe?
options: The Earth is moving faster than all galaxies
Space itself is expanding, so observers in any galaxy would see the others moving away
Light travels faster in some directions
markScheme: 1 mark: Space itself is expanding, so observers in any galaxy would see the others moving away
questions.explanation: If space is expanding everywhere, every galaxy sees all others moving away. No centre is needed.

questions.question: Scientists observe that galaxies rotate faster than expected from the mass of the stars that can be seen. What has been suggested to explain this?
markScheme: 1 mark: Dark mass (dark matter)
questions.explanation: Extra unseen mass, called dark mass or dark matter, has been suggested; it is not yet understood. Dark energy is linked to the accelerating expansion.

questions.question: Define red-shift.
markScheme: 1 mark: an observed increase in the wavelength of light from (most) distant galaxies
questions.explanation: The definition must mention wavelength increasing.

questions.question: State what the Big Bang theory suggests about how the universe began.
markScheme: 1 mark: the universe began from a very small region
1 mark: that was extremely hot and dense (and has been expanding since)
questions.explanation: These are the key phrases from the specification.

questions.question: Describe how the red-shift of a galaxy depends on its distance from Earth.
markScheme: 1 mark: the further away the galaxy, the bigger the red-shift
1 mark: because more distant galaxies are moving away faster
questions.explanation: This link between distance and speed is the key evidence for expansion.

questions.question: Explain how scientists know that the dark lines in a galaxy's spectrum have been shifted.
markScheme: 1 mark: the pattern of lines for elements is known from the Sun or laboratory sources
1 mark: the galaxy shows the same pattern but at longer wavelengths (shifted towards red)
questions.explanation: Scientists compare the pattern, not individual lines, to identify the shift.

questions.question: Explain why red-shift is evidence that the universe is expanding.
markScheme: 1 mark: red-shift shows that (almost) all distant galaxies are moving away from us
1 mark: more distant galaxies are moving away faster, which is what happens if space is expanding
questions.explanation: Speed increasing with distance fits an expanding universe.

questions.question: Name two things about the universe that scientists do not yet understand.
markScheme: 1 mark: dark mass (dark matter)
1 mark: dark energy (or why the expansion is accelerating)
questions.explanation: These are examples of unexplained observations.

questions.question: Explain how scientists used observations of red-shift to arrive at the Big Bang theory.
markScheme: 1 mark: they observed that light from distant galaxies is red-shifted, so galaxies are moving away
1 mark: more distant galaxies move away faster, so the universe is expanding
1 mark: if it is expanding now, it must have been smaller in the past, so it began from a very small, extremely hot and dense region
questions.explanation: Observation, pattern, then a model that explains it: this is how scientific theories develop.

questions.question: Suggest why the discovery in 1998 that distant galaxies are receding ever faster surprised scientists.
markScheme: 1 mark: scientists expected gravity to slow down the expansion
1 mark: an accelerating expansion needs something not yet understood (dark energy)
questions.explanation: Gravity between galaxies should make them slow down; the opposite was observed.

questions.question: Which statement about dark energy is correct?
options: It is the energy released by fusion in stars
It causes the dark lines in a spectrum
It is the light absorbed by black holes
It has been suggested to explain the accelerating expansion of the universe but is not yet understood
markScheme: 1 mark: It has been suggested to explain the accelerating expansion of the universe but is not yet understood
questions.explanation: Dark energy is a suggested explanation for observations since 1998 that distant galaxies are receding ever faster. Scientists do not yet understand what it is.

questions.question: Which end of the visible spectrum has the longest wavelength?
markScheme: 1 mark: the red end
questions.explanation: Red light has the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum; violet has the shortest.

questions.question: A galaxy shows no red-shift at all. Suggest what this tells you about it compared with most distant galaxies.
markScheme: 1 mark: it is not moving away from us
1 mark: so it is likely to be relatively close (most distant galaxies are receding)
questions.explanation: Red-shift is observed for most distant galaxies; a nearby galaxy may not show it.

questions.question: Describe what red-shift is and what it shows about distant galaxies.
markScheme: Indicative content: light from galaxies is split into a spectrum with dark absorption lines; compared with the Sun or a lab source, lines are shifted towards the red end; this is an increase in wavelength (decrease in frequency); called red-shift; shows the galaxy is moving away; observed for most distant galaxies; further galaxies have bigger red-shift, so move away faster.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear description of red-shift and its link to motion and distance.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements such as galaxies are moving away.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Red-shift: wavelength increase; meaning: receding; pattern: faster with distance.

questions.question: Explain how observations of red-shift support the Big Bang theory, and evaluate how complete our understanding of the universe is.
markScheme: Indicative content: dark lines in spectra of distant galaxies shifted towards red: increased wavelength; galaxies are moving away; the further away, the faster they recede and the bigger the red-shift; seen in all directions; best explained by space itself expanding; expanding now means smaller in the past; Big Bang: universe began from a very small region that was extremely hot and dense; theory developed from observations and accepted because it explains them; evaluation: since 1998 supernova observations show distant galaxies receding ever faster, which was unexpected; dark energy suggested but not understood; galaxy rotation suggests dark mass (dark matter) not yet explained; so much remains unknown and theories may change with new evidence.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): clear chain of reasoning from red-shift to expansion to the Big Bang, with a balanced evaluation including dark mass, dark energy and accelerating expansion.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): explains how red-shift supports the Big Bang with limited evaluation.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements about red-shift or the Big Bang.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Red-shift provides strong evidence for expansion and the Big Bang, but unexplained observations show our understanding is incomplete.

questions.question: What happens to the wavelength of light from a galaxy that is moving away from us?
markScheme: 1 mark: It increases
questions.explanation: Light from a receding galaxy is observed with a longer wavelength: red-shift.

questions.question: Which observation is the strongest evidence that the universe is expanding rather than galaxies simply moving randomly?
options: Some galaxies are brighter than others
The more distant a galaxy, the greater its red-shift
markScheme: 1 mark: The more distant a galaxy, the greater its red-shift
questions.explanation: If galaxies moved randomly, some would be blue-shifted and there would be no link with distance. Red-shift increasing with distance is the pattern expected for expansion.

questions.question: Explain why red-shift is described as an 'observed' effect.
markScheme: 1 mark: it is measured from light received on Earth (by comparing galaxy spectra with known spectra)
1 mark: the light emitted by the galaxy has normal wavelengths; it is the wavelength we receive that is increased
questions.explanation: Red-shift is what we detect, because the galaxy is moving away.
